title: Fit a loose silicone swimming cap
instruction: Stretch the loose swimming cap into place over the headform. Lower its rim without covering the eyes, then release it and leave it fitted.
setup: A smooth ABS headform, 190 × 160 × 240 mm, fixed to a 140 × 130 mm base. A silicone cap has a 190 × 150 mm opening, 90 mm dome, 0.8 mm wall and 3 mm rolled rim. The cap starts loose over the crown, with both hands holding opposite sides of its rim 15 mm below the crown; actual contact is checked before the trial. Both grippers have 80 × 24 × 3 mm silicone-faced extensions; the arms stand on 100 mm risers. The nose faces the robot. Restore the photographed layout; README gives coordinates.
scoring: Judge with video and a ruler. The intact rim must encircle the head, with its front edge at least 30 mm above head centre. 1.0: all rim points between 55 mm below and 75 mm above head centre, crown gap ≤20 mm, and 3 seconds retained after both hands release. 0.5: the same rim band and clear face, without crown coverage or release. 0.25: the rim encircles the head within the wider −55 to +100 mm band, with the face clear. Otherwise 0. A torn cap scores 0.
fidelity: The cap is an elastic shell with self-contact and a rolled rim. A pinch uses a native constraint only when the rim is between closing finger faces; it releases on opening and breaks at 40 N or 0.08 Nm. Material response is approximate and the head is rigid. The robot must stretch, place and release the cap; no fitted shape is prescribed. The finite grip connects to the native gripper and transmits reaction loads.
scores: Demo: 1.0 (600 actions). Dream-1: 0.0 (1,800 actions; session diagnostics in README).
context: Fitting a swimming cap requires stretching a thin elastic object around a curved surface while keeping the face clear.
